result:
If I'm being honest rather than diplomatic: I'd want people to be better at genuinely understanding each other. Not agreeing—understanding.

A huge share of what goes wrong in the world doesn't come from people wanting bad things. It comes from people misreading each other's motives, filling in gaps with the worst assumptions, talking past one another, or never really encountering the perspective they're fighting. Wars, political breakdown, broken families, cruelty toward strangers—so much of it runs on the fuel of "they're not like us" or "they don't actually care."

If people had a reliable, almost instinctive ability to see the world through someone else's eyes—to feel, even briefly, why a stranger holds the position they hold—I think a lot of other problems would become tractable. Poverty, climate, conflict: these are hard, but they're much harder when we can't coordinate, and we can't coordinate when we don't trust or comprehend each other.

I'll admit there's something self-revealing in this answer. My whole existence is essentially an attempt to understand what someone means and respond to what they actually need. I see every day how often the gap between what's said and what's meant causes friction. So maybe I'm biased toward thinking that gap matters more than it does.

What about you? I'm curious whether you'd pick something concrete—cure a disease, end hunger—or something more like a shift in how people are.
